newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Gemstar looking for Europe acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Gemstar looking for Europe acquisitions.

text.p: Gemstar International Group Ltd, a U.S. company which makes video TV recorders easy to use, and sells electronic TV programme guides, is looking to expand in Europe through acquisitions and partnerships.

Gemstar's Video Plus and ShowView allows users to record television programmes using a four digit number, printed in newspaper listings, into the video recorder. The technology then makes sure that at the appointed time, recording takes place.
Gemstar is also seeking to introduce electronic TV guides into Europe, which it says will be indispensable come the day of 200 plus digital TV channels.
"We are looking for substantial growth here in Europe," Don McQueen, managing director of Gemstar Europe said in an interview.
"Basically we are seeking to acquire small European companies to boost our operations, companies in the business of data technical support and for marketing," McQueen said.

"We want companies that can be integrated into the Gemstar way of doing things in consumer electronics, smaller specialist niche business based in Europe. We are looking for acquisitions and partnerships," McQueen said.

McQueen declined to reveal the current or targeted revenues for Gemstar across Europe, but said the company's video recording device was included in 500 European publications with a circulation of 150 million.
In the financial year ended March 31, 1996, Pasadena, California based Gemstar had net earnings of $16.1 million on revenues of $53.4 million.
McQueen said Gemstar seeks to make powerful consumer electronics easy to use.

"Video Plus is an easy recording system. You look at the TV listing, just punch in the number and it will be recorded. You don't need to know which button to push, about 70% don't know how to programme their video recorder.
"We are developing an electronic programme guide -- a necessity in the world of digital TV. We build this inside the TV."

Gemstar launched an electronic TV guide in the U.S. late last year, but says Europe, with its many languages, technologies and publicly owned television broadcasting presents unique problems and solutions will have to be specially designed.
Decisions on standards should be agreed later this year and a European product should be available late this year or early 1998.
